title: Distilling the Knowledge in a Neural Network
hook: A big model's softened probabilities say more than hard labels - they reveal how classes relate, so training a small model to mimic them transfers knowledge a one-hot target never could.
key_points: Compresses a large model or ensemble into a single smaller model that is easier to deploy.
Trains the student on the teacher's 'soft' output probabilities, softened with a temperature, not just hard labels.
Soft targets carry extra information about how classes relate to each other.
Showed results on MNIST and improved a heavily used commercial acoustic model.
Introduces 'specialist' models, trainable in parallel, for confusable fine-grained classes.
content_html: Geoffrey Hinton, Oriol Vinyals, and Jeff Dean introduced knowledge distillation in March 2015 as a way to compress the knowledge of a large model or ensemble into a single smaller model that is easier to deploy. Building on Caruana's model-compression idea with a different technique, they showed that what a big model "knows" lives in more than just its top prediction.
extra_html:
How it works

Instead of training the small student only on hard labels, you train it on the large teacher's "soft" output probabilities, softened with a temperature. Those soft targets carry extra information about how classes relate to each other - for example, that a particular digit is much more likely to be confused with one digit than another. The authors also introduce "specialist" models, trainable in parallel, that focus on confusable fine-grained classes.

Why it matters

Hinton, Vinyals, and Dean demonstrated the approach on MNIST and used it to improve a heavily used commercial acoustic model. The idea - have a small, deployable model mimic a larger one's softened outputs - became a foundational recipe for model compression and underpins later work like DistilBERT.

related.title: DistilBERT: Smaller, Faster, Cheaper, Lighter
related.hook: Distill during pre-training instead of after, and you get a general-purpose language model that is 40% smaller and 60% faster while keeping 97% of BERT's understanding.

related.title: Sequence-Level Knowledge Distillation
related.hook: Match the teacher's whole output sequence, not just word-by-word probabilities, and the student translation model can drop beam search while running about 10x faster.

related.title: Making Distillation Cheap: Offline Top-K Logits and a Fused Chunked KL Loss
related.hook: You don't need the teacher in memory. Cache its top-K logits once, then train the student against the cache — same loss, ~29% faster per step, and 4x the context on one GPU.
